title: Large-scale single-cell cloning of genome-edited cultured human cells by On-chip SPiS
author: Takahashi, Miyaoka
materials: Corning® Matrigel® Growth Factor Reduced Basement Membrane Matrix

This section describes the design of gRNAs and short single-stranded donor DNAs for genome editing.1.Design of gRNAs and single-stranded donor DNAs for single nucleotide substitutions.a.Design a gRNA using Cas-Designer14 (http://www.rgenome.net/cas-designer/) or CRISPRdirect15 (http://crispr.dbcls.jp/) in a gene of interest.Note: The cut site should be within 10 bp from the single-nucleotide substitution. It is also desirable to locate the nucleotide substitutions within the gRNA or PAM sequence to avoid re-cleavage of edited alleles by Cas9.Note: If there is no cut site available for SpCas9, the Cas9 orthologs or engineered Cas9 variants with different PAM sequences from SpCas9 can be used (e.g., SaCas9,16 SpCas9-NG17).b.The single-stranded donor DNA should be 60 nucleotides (nt) in length with the single-nucleotide substitution in the middle (5′-29-nt homologous sequence + 1-nt substitution + 30-nt homologous sequence-3′) (Figure 1A). The 60-nt single-stranded donor DNA can induce substitutions of up to 2 nucleotides. We recommend to extend the single-stranded donor DNA length when substitutions of 3 nucleotides or more are intended.Alternatives: Other gRNA design software programs can also be used (e.g., CHOPCHOP18 [http://chopchop.cbu.uib.no/] and Benchling [https://www.benchling.com/crispr]).Note: The human U6 Promoter in px458-HypaCas9 requires a guanine (G) base to initiate efficient transcription (Figure 1B). If the sequence does not begin with a G, add a G at the 5′ end to make a 21-nt gRNA. The purification grade of oligonucleotides for both donor and gRNA is reversed-phase chromatography (RPC).Figure 1Design of donor DNA and cloning of a gRNA into px458-HypaCas9 for editing RBM20(A) Design of single-stranded donor DNA for R636S (c.1906C>A) point mutagenesis in RBM20. Red nucleotides indicate the substituted nucleotides. The black and red underlines indicate the gRNA and PAM sequences, respectively.(B) Cloning of a gRNA for point mutagenesis. A cytosine (red) was substituted, and a 5′ guanine (blue) of the annealed 20-bp oligonucleotides was required for optimal transcription driven by the human U6 promoter.2.Cloning of gRNAs.Note: Our protocol for gRNA cloning into the px458-HypaCas9 plasmid is a slightly modified version of the one used for pX330-based plasmids established by Dr. Feng Zhang (https://www.addgene.org/crispr/zhang/#spcas9).19 The original protocol can be applied here too.a.Digestion and dephosphorylation of px458-HypaCas9.i.Order px458-HypaCas9 (#190604) from Addgene.ii.px458-HypaCas9 is digested by BpiI (BbsI) and dephosphorylated by Fast AP (alkaline phosphatase) as shown in below Table.Restriction and dephosphorylation solution.ReagentFinal concentrationAmountpx458-HypaCas9 plasmid (1 μg/μL)50 ng/μL1.0 μLFastDigest BpiI1x1.0 μLFastAP1 unit/20 μL1.0 μLFastDigest Green Buffer (10x)1x2.0 μLMQWN/A15.0 μLTotalN/A20.0 μLiii.After running the digested plasmid on a 1% agarose gel electrophoresis, the band is cut out, and the DNA is purified with a common gel purification kit (e.g., FastGene Gel/PCR Extraction Kit), and eluted with 20 μL of MQW. steps.title: Design gRNA and donor ssDNA
steps.instruction: Use Cas‑Designer or CRISPRdirect (or CHOPCHOP, Benchling) to design a gRNA whose cut site lies within 10 bp of the desired single‑nucleotide substitution; place the substitution inside the gRNA or PAM if possible. If no SpCas9 site exists, consider SaCas9 or SpCas9‑NG. Order a 60‑nt single‑stranded donor DNA (29 nt homology‑upstream + 1 nt substitution + 30 nt homology‑downstream); extend length for ≥3 nt changes. Ensure the U6‑promoter‑driven gRNA starts with a G (add a 5′‑G to make a 21‑nt guide if needed). Order all oligos (gRNA and donor) purified by reversed‑phase chromatography.

steps.title: Clone gRNA into px458‑HypaCas9 plasmid
steps.instruction: Perform plasmid digestion, gel purification, oligo phosphorylation/annealing, ligation, bacterial transformation, colony growth, plasmid miniprep and sequence verification.

substeps.instruction: Digest 50 ng/µL px458‑HypaCas9 (Addgene #190604) with 1 µL FastDigest BpiI and 1 µL FastAP in 2 µL 10× FastDigest Green Buffer, add 15 µL MQW to 20 µL total; incubate as recommended.
Run the digest on a 1 % agarose gel, excise the linearized band, purify with a gel extraction kit and elute in 20 µL MQW (expected ~20 ng/µL).

Order two complementary oligos: forward with 5′‑CACC (or CACCG if a G is required) overhang, reverse with 5′‑AAAC overhang. Prepare 10 µL phosphorylation/annealing mix containing 1 µL 100 µM forward (10 µM final), 1 µL 100 µM reverse (10 µM), 1 µL 1× T4 DNA Ligase Reaction Buffer, 0.5 µL T4 PNK (5 U/10 µL), 6.5 µL MQW. Incubate 37 °C 30 min, then 95 °C 5 min, ramp down to 25 °C at 5 °C/min. Dilute the reaction 1:250 with MQW.

Ligate: combine 0.5 µL diluted annealed oligos (0.1 µM), 0.5 µL linearized plasmid (10 ng/µL), 1 µL Ligation High ver.2 (2×) and MQW to 2 µL total. Incubate at room temperature 30 min, then place on ice.
Add 2 µL ligation to 10 µL chemically competent DH5‑Alpha cells in a 1.5 mL tube, keep on ice 10 min, heat‑shock 37 °C 40 s, return to ice 1 min, add 750 µL SOC, shake 37 °C 30 min.
Plate 100‑200 µL on LB‑ampicillin (100 µg/mL) plates, incubate 37 °C overnight (12–20 h). Pick several colonies, grow each in 1.5 mL LB‑amp (100 µg/mL) overnight at 37 °C.

Perform a miniprep (e.g., Zyppy Plasmid Miniprep Kit), measure DNA concentration spectrophotometrically, and confirm the gRNA insert by Sanger sequencing using the primers listed in the key resources table.

steps.title: Thaw and maintain HEK293T cells
steps.instruction: Thaw a frozen vial (~2 × 10⁶ cells) in a 37 °C water bath, mix the cells with 10 mL PBS in a 15 mL tube, centrifuge 280 × g 3 min at room temperature, aspirate supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 10 mL growth medium and transfer to a 10‑cm dish. When confluent (typically 4–5 days), passage at a 1:20 ratio without changing medium between passages.

steps.title: Prepare conditioned medium
steps.instruction: From confluent 10‑cm dishes, remove growth medium, wash once with 10 mL PBS, add 1 mL 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA and incubate 37 °C 3 min, then add 9 mL growth medium and resuspend cells. Transfer 0.5 mL of this suspension to a new 10‑cm dish and add 10 mL fresh growth medium (this dish will yield ~10 mL conditioned medium, sufficient for one 96‑well plate). After 3–5 days culture, collect the medium into a 50‑mL tube, centrifuge 280 × g 3 min, transfer the clarified supernatant to a fresh tube and store at 4 °C (up to 2 months).

steps.title: Prepare growth media
steps.instruction: Prepare two formulations: (1) Growth medium: DMEM 1× 500 mL, FBS 10 % 50 mL, Penicillin‑Streptomycin 1 % 5 mL (total 555 mL). (2) Growth medium 2: DMEM 1× 500 mL, FBS 20 % 100 mL, Penicillin‑Streptomycin 1 % 5 mL (total 605 mL). Store both at 4 °C up to 2 months.

steps.title: Coat 12‑well plate with Matrigel
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Matrigel solution to each well of a 12‑well plate, incubate at 37 °C for at least 1 h to allow coating.

steps.title: Seed cells in 12‑well plate
steps.instruction: Detach HEK293T cells with 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA, count, remove the Matrigel solution from the coated wells, seed 2 × 10⁵ cells per well in 500 µL growth medium, and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ overnight (12–24 h).

steps.title: Prepare transfection mixtures
steps.instruction: Adjust px458‑HypaCas9 plasmid to 1 µg/µL (1 000 ng/µL) and donor ssDNA to 100 ng/µL. For each well, prepare Mixture 1: 40 µL Opti‑MEM + 2.4 µL Lipofectamine 2000 (total 42.4 µL). Prepare Mixture 2: 40 µL Opti‑MEM, 7.2 µL px458‑HypaCas9 (providing 20 ng), 0.8 µL donor ssDNA (80 ng), and MQW to a final volume of 48 µL (total DNA per well 800 ng). Add 40 µL of Mixture 1 and 40 µL of Mixture 2 to each well, mix gently and incubate at room temperature 20 min.

steps.title: Transfect cells
steps.instruction: After the 20‑min incubation, drip 80 µL of the combined transfection solution onto each well of the 12‑well plate containing the seeded HEK293T cells. Incubate further and observe EGFP fluorescence the next day to assess transfection efficiency.

steps.title: Coat 96‑well plates with Matrigel
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL Matrigel solution to each well of a 96‑well plate, then incubate the plate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ overnight (3–24 h) before single‑cell dispensing.
